title: How the Stretch Is Measured where a Host's Reading Runs Ahead of the Records
content:
The miles a reading the host reports take off the interval are not counted before an odometer record dated the handling date and naming the condition record its reading was taken from stands on the vehicle's condition record.

A reading the host reports is recorded on the vehicle's condition record whatever distance stands between it and the reading the most recent telematics odometer record carries, and that distance is settled by the way the reported stretch is measured rather than by holding the reading back.

On a Keyturn Vehicle Listing the reported stretch is measured as follows.

1. Where the odometer standing on the listing is more than 75 miles above the highest reading standing on the vehicle's odometer records and a completed inspection dated within 7 calendar days of the handling date stands on the condition record, the reported stretch is measured from that highest standing reading to the odometer standing on the listing.

2. Where the odometer standing on the listing is more than 75 miles above that highest standing reading and no such inspection stands, the reported stretch is measured from that highest standing reading and then cut back by the 75 mile margin the marketplace queries rather than charges.

3. Otherwise the reported stretch is measured from the reading the vehicle's most recent telematics odometer record carries to the odometer standing on the listing.

### Worked on hypothetical records

*An odometer of 62000 miles standing on the listing against a highest standing reading of 61000 miles.* The reported reading is 1000 miles above the highest standing reading, which is more than 75 miles, so one of the first two clauses governs. With a completed inspection dated 3 calendar days before the handling date, the reported stretch is 1000 miles. With the most recent completed inspection dated 20 calendar days before the handling date, the reported stretch is 1000 miles cut back by the 75 mile margin, that is 925 miles.

*The same listing against a highest standing reading of 61960 miles.* The reported reading is 40 miles above it, which is not more than 75 miles, so the third clause governs and the reported stretch is measured from the most recent telematics odometer record.

*At the boundary.* A reported reading exactly 75 miles above the highest standing reading is not more than 75 miles above it and falls to the third clause; one 76 miles above it is on the first or the second.
